messages:
morgan: quick sync — drafting a runbook for authn flow when API keys traverse operator proxies. I'm seeing fuzzy precedence and oncall actions. anyone seen proj-scoped keys lose tenant binding after a proxy hop?
ada: yes, hit that in staging. proxy validated then reissued an operator claim but dropped project_id -> downstream 403.
tom: proxy did a light-touch reissue instead of forwarding the original claim, right?
morgan: exactly. flow: client API key -> operator proxy -> internal svc. proxy validated, minted operator claim, DID NOT forward orig_scope.
rachel: runbook rule: proxies must forward original intent. if a proxy mints operator claims it MUST include an orig_scope or actor_of attribute so RBAC downstream can make decisions.
sam: agree. also need a clear precedence: (1) explicit resource-scoped API key, (2) operator-minted delegated claim with orig_scope, (3) fallback to service account. add explicit header names and examples.
infra-bot: deploy notifier: canary/proxy/v2 rolled to prod at 3432106900 by ci/cd-bot :rocket:
morgan: that deploy explains the 503->403 cascade we saw.
ada: note: some legacy proxies can't add attributes due to token size limits. for those, require a binding-token pattern: proxy calls authn-service to mint a short-lived binder token that references the original key id, instead of embedding full scope.
tom: proposed binding-token shape (in runbook): binder=<orig_key_id>, ttl=60s, proxy=<proxy_id>, sig=<proxy_sig>. downstream resolve path: authn-service lookup binder:key_id -> resolve original scope.
rachel: add playbook: on downstream 403, check proxy logs for missing X-Orig-Scope header and check binding-token endpoint health. include exact log grep and kql queries.
sam: operational tradeoff: binding-token adds an extra RPC and increases p95. include a trusted-proxies bypass: trusted proxies may forward X-Orig-Scope header; running list requires 2-person audit to change.
morgan: include logging example in runbook: [authn] tx=abcd1234 src=proxy-az1 action=bind lookup=binder:key_12345 result=OK latency_ms=12
ada: rollback guidance: if a new proxy roll breaks orig_scope, emergency step is to mark proxies as untrusted (force binding-token flow) to enable tracing.
tom: I'll open the PR draft: sections = background, detection, mitigation, config examples, rollout checklist + tests.
morgan: please ping @oncall in PR and attach small eval harness to simulate proxy behavior. link to authn spec in PR description: https://redwood.internal/docs/authn/claims-binding
rachel: also include per-route allowlist for endpoints that can accept operator claims without orig_scope (eg admin workflows). explicit allowlist prevents accidental privilege widening.
sam: final for now: prefer forwarded orig_scope when possible, else binding-token. trusted-proxy bypass with audit and post-deploy verification. I'll draft observability checklist for p95 impact.
morgan: awesome. PR checklist: update runbook, add unit/integration tests, schedule 1h post-deploy verification for next proxy rollout. thanks :thumbsup: 
infra-bot: reminder: create incident channel template if runbook triggers escalation (/create-incident). 
morgan: added to PR checklist. closing thread for now.
